FILE: J_63_keyboard_service_owns_shortcuts.md Keyboard shortcuts are currently registered from React components (`.tsx` files), through a mix of `KeyboardShortcutService` bindings and raw `window` `keydown` listeners. Each handler decides on its own whether it applies, using `viewMode` checks, focus checks, or nothing at all. The keyboard service must become the one place that handles keyboard shortcuts, including their registration: * Services own shortcut registration, not components. No shortcut registration in `.tsx` files. * A global keyboard service owns the app-wide shortcuts (for example Ctrl+S commit, global search), not a component. * One sub keyboard service per view: dashboard (cards), text, stats, diagram, ... * The global keyboard service monitors which view is active and loads the matching sub keyboard service. Only the sub keyboard service of the active view handles keys. md² appears eligible, but I recommend submitting it under **Agent Infrastructure → Multi-Agent Orchestration**, not **AI-Native IDEs**.

The IDE category is defined as full development environments offering code generation, chat, and debugging. md² is positioned as an orchestration workspace around Codex CLI and Claude Code, Markdown feature cards, and isolated Git worktrees. That closely matches existing entries such as Conductor, Vibe Kanban, and Kagan. [See the list’s categories](https://github.com/jamesmurdza/awesome-ai-devtools#multi-agent-orchestration).

1. Fork `jamesmurdza/awesome-ai-devtools`.
2. Add one entry to `README.md` under `### Multi-Agent Orchestration`.
3. Open a pull request titled:
   `Add md² to Multi-Agent Orchestration`
4. Complete the repository’s checklist:
   - The tool uses AI.
   - It is developer-focused.
   - The description is clear and unambiguous.
   - The description matches other entries’ style.

Those are the only published submission requirements. Self-submissions are not prohibited. [Contribution rules](https://github.com/jamesmurdza/awesome-ai-devtools/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).

Runs coding agents in parallel Git worktrees with a Kanban-style dashboard, conversation history, merge workflows, reusable actions, diagrams, and token and cost tracking.

This description is supported by the current [md² README](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2), including the downloadable Windows installer, agent integrations, worktree management, and documentation.
